knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.1.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) Define bias of an estimator. (2) How does MSE relate to bias and variance? (3) In one sentence each, what do efficiency and consistency mean?
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Bias is E[θ̂] − θ (CMP form). MSE = Var(θ̂) + (bias)² under standard decomposition. Efficiency compares variance (or MSE) relative to a benchmark; consistency concerns convergence in probability as sample size grows.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.1.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Estimator A is unbiased with Var(A)=4/n. Estimator B has Bias(B)=1/n and Var(B)=1/n. (1) Give MSE(A) and MSE(B). (2) For large n, which has smaller MSE? (3) Refuse: 'Unbiased always beats biased' and 'consistency means the estimator is unbiased.'
knowledge_checks.body: Distinguish bias, MSE, consistency on a concrete claim.
knowledge_checks.explanation: MSE = bias² + variance; consistency ≠ unbiasedness; a biased estimator can have smaller MSE.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) MSE(A)=4/n; MSE(B)=(1/n)² + 1/n = 1/n² + 1/n. (2) For large n, MSE(B)≈1/n < 4/n = MSE(A), so B is preferred on MSE. (3) Refuse: unbiasedness is not MSE optimality; consistency is large-sample concentration on the true value, not the same as unbiasedness.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating unbiasedness as automatically best, or equating consistency with unbiasedness.
success_criteria: Computes both MSEs and compares them for large n.
Refuses conflating unbiasedness with MSE optimality and with consistency.
